Edition II continuity and provenance note. The preceding edition's complete accessible chapter is carried forward rather than summarised. This chapter remains subject to future creator revisions and the pending ChatGPT-export comparison. ## Edition II continuity guardrails - This is the evidence register, not the chronological event record. The Campaign Chronicle governs when something happened and to whom. - Distinguish the mine's old physical architecture from theories about an interconnected network; distinguish Edrik's reported breach from direct proof. - Darrik and Harnel independently heard three irregular knocks, but disagreed on whispering and hum. Neither witnessed a visible passageway or entity. - The dark drainage stone and pale-grey workshop retaining granite are different samples. No proven link, intelligent response or familiar ancestry is established. - Hadrik's repository register has Varric, an administrative custodian and obscured third name. The identity and contents remain unverified. - The sealed wooden materials case, removed authority piece, old fourth official, restricted report, other sealed sites and Veyron's intentions remain distinct unresolved leads. Never combine them without actual evidence. - The historical dating of Silence Below is inconsistent between two reference formulations; see issue C-02 in the edition index. Direct source: Open Mysteries & Research Leads. Historical source: The Eryndor World Bible. --- ## Complete topic reference — preserved from the preceding edition This page is an index of unresolved questions, evidence and active research threads. It is not a replacement for the Campaign Chronicle. The chronicle records when something happened; this page records what remains unresolved, what evidence exists and who is pursuing each lead. ## Evidence discipline For every mystery: - Record direct observations separately from interpretations. - Attribute testimony and documents to their sources. - Preserve contradictions and uncertainty. - Do not infer a cause from correlation alone. - Do not treat a lack of evidence as proof of absence. - Keep independent mysteries independent unless evidence establishes a connection. - Update a lead when new evidence arrives; do not silently rewrite earlier observations. ## The eastern mine and the Hall Beneath the Mountain \Active unresolved mystery\ ### Established background - The eastern mine was officially sealed 63 years ago after reported collapses. - Public maps show six levels; Borin Ashmantle's older survey shows nine. - The lower galleries contain deliberately engineered construction older than the mine. - Beneath level nine lies the Hall Beneath the Mountain and a sealed stone doorway. - The mine was built over an older First Throne structure. - A margin note dated three days before closure reads: “Sound observed beyond the western wall. No machinery identified.” - Thrain Coppervein, the chief surveyor, disappeared first. Orik Feldspar, the structural engineer who supervised the sealing, disappeared six weeks later. Dorin Blackmantle, a royal inspector, was last recorded entering the Crownward district. No known bodies or funerals; their families reportedly received no official compensation. - Borin Ashmantle was an apprentice engineer at the sealing and helped close the lower access. He retained portions of the original survey. ### Day 19 survey, witness and allegation chain — recovered early transcript - 7:35 AM, Borin's own testimony: The sealed mine had formerly yielded excellent iron; the collapse story was, in Borin's view, a cover for a discovery beneath the oldest galleries. Borin had helped seal the lower access as an apprentice; he had not entered the chamber. He said witnesses were ordered silent and that three dissenting engineers disappeared. These assertions are not direct testimony from the vanished engineers. - 8:05 AM, the original private survey: Borin showed Gloin three surviving parchments retained from his part of the engineering work, in a wooden case from his home. The six-versus-nine-level contrast, precise engineering, Hall Beneath the Mountain inscription, sealed doorway and marginal note dated three days before closure are visible documentary evidence as described by the original narrator; the cause of the recorded sound was not established. Borin translated the chamber name. - Missing engineers: Borin named Thrain (first to vanish), Orik (six weeks later) and Dorin (last seen entering Crownward); he said no bodies, funerals or official compensation were known. Borin knew Orik and said Orik had three children. Edrik later challenged Borin's assertion that Thrain was dead, citing no official death record. Neither statement proves Thrain's present fate. - 27 days before Day 19: According to Borin, a Royal Mining Office visitor asked specifically about a Hall Beneath the Mountain survey and claimed night watchmen had heard three knocks behind the sealed door. Borin had not heard this himself. The later 8:44 visitor was identified as Edrik Voss. - 8:44 AM, eavesdropped Royal Mining Office visit: Gloin hid behind workshop barrels; Borin concealed the survey case under a loose floorboard. Edrik arrived with an unnamed armed royal guard. Edrik said a western wall breach had occurred eleven nights earlier, that “something came through”, and that watchmen heard knocks and unintelligible voices. He also claimed King Durgan IV had not been informed and the investigation was managed by Lord Chancellor Veyron. Gloin directly heard Edrik's claims but neither Gloin nor Borin is thereby a witness to a breach, crossing or entity. Edrik's account is not a confirmed finding. - After the visit: Borin showed Gloin a hammer-and-crown mark near the western wall on the survey and identified the same design in an old history book as the First Throne's seal. This is evidence of an attributed mark and source text, not proof that a particular door contains a living presence or that an entire ancient network is operating. - 9:35 AM knowledge boundary: Hadrik had just met Gloin for the first time and had not yet been told about the survey. Borin possessed the original sheets. Later reports and Day 22 watchmen's independent accounts must remain distinct from Edrik's Day 19 allegations. ### Day 19, 3:06 PM — the original request to Maela (newly dated source) At the Silver Anvil, with Gloin, Borin and Hadrik present, a young courier handed Maela a message from the Royal Mining Office. Maela read that the office wished to commission a runesmith to inspect old defensive inscriptions at the eastern mine because the surviving structural plans were incomplete, and offered a generous fee. Asked who authorised it, Maela identified Lord Chancellor Veyron's office from the parchment. Borin stiffened, and Maela suspected a connection to the group's discoveries. At that exact moment, Maela explicitly said “I haven't accepted.” This receipt of an offer must not be conflated with the later conditional acceptance described in the mine-inspection planning records, the later list of authorised technical materials, or the actual Day 22 inspection participants. The complete intervening discussion and timing of acceptance are not yet recovered. The request and stated authorising office were in a message; they do not establish malicious intent, Veyron's complete private reasoning or the King's knowledge. The archived Day 19 material-screening scene happened at the Silver Anvil before the messenger arrived. ### Day 20 afternoon — testimony circulation, Varric lead and limits (new source) The recovered Day 20 text starts after an unseen earlier investigation involving Edda Coppervein and Crownward documents. A retrospective accomplishment ledger states that Gloin had visited Thrain's descendants, obtained a copy of the note attributed to Thrain, and identified Varric Stonehelm, Examiner-General at the time of the mine sealing, as the official who authorised Dorin Blackmantle's appointment. The note itself remains an attributed family document; this summary establishes what the story told Gloin, not that Varric knew of an incomplete authority mechanism or ordered wrongdoing. How the records were inspected and their wording await earlier Day 20 footage. Orik's alleged interest in opening the sealed door and possible opposition to Thrain are unverified accounts. At Day 20 3:55 PM, Gloin shared the note and Varric lead with Hadrik. Hadrik read the transcription twice and took a copy for his records. Hadrik said Thrain may have removed the authority component to prevent operation and insisted that Orik's reasons still mattered. He remembered Varric as a senior official and promised to check whether he left the Royal Mining Office in unusual circumstances. The outcome of this particular promise was not supplied in this scene. This must be reconciled with later archive/repository research rather than treated as immediate discovery. At Day 20 4:40 PM, Gloin showed Maela the attributed note. She read the words that the authority piece “cannot be allowed to remain connected” and interpreted the removal as deliberate. An incomplete authority mechanism might explain contemporary confusion, but she was not willing to claim reactivation of a listening network by the reported breach without examining the original arrangement; she made a note for the later inspection. This is interpretation, not demonstration of causality. Knowledge boundaries: Both Hadrik and Maela know the Day 20 note and the related disclosed discoveries by the end of their meetings. This does not mean Hadrik learned Maela and Gloin's separate Day 22 resonance readings, stone comparisons or watchman interviews; he still had not been briefed on those at the Day 22 11:25 AM pause. The original note stays with the descendants; copies and later research are distinct. ### Thrain's note and missing authority piece A parchment note attributed by Thrain's family to Thrain Coppervein reads: > The lower chambers are not empty.
Orik believes the resonance is structural. I no longer agree.
The western wall responds to the listening stones. Three knocks have been recorded twice now.
I have removed the authority piece from its housing. It cannot be allowed to remain connected. The note is undated. Edda Coppervein says the family attributes the handwriting to Thrain. Edda recalls that he protected something wrapped in dark cloth. Her grandmother remembered Thrain saying Orik wanted to open the door while he wanted to keep it closed. Borin independently recalled a one-hand-sized iron object marked with the Hammer and Crown, wrapped in dark cloth, shortly before the sealing. He never saw it again. The object's identity and present location remain open. The sealed system appears to have three concentric mechanisms: 1. An outer pressure regulator that distributes force through the mountain. 2. A middle containment barrier. 3. An inner authority mechanism. The removed authority component may be a key, attunement mark or control element. Its precise function is unknown. Do not assume that reinserting it would open the door or that it is necessarily the only missing component. ### Historical context — the Silence Below Records from roughly 3,240–3,160 years before the Seven Thrones describe rhythmic hammering from below, failures of magical lights in the Unlit Halls, reports of movement in darkness and a final sealing. An old warning reads: > Let no descendant mistake the silence of the deep for the absence of what dwells within. The historical accounts do not prove what lies behind the present mine door or that the same presence remains. Hadrik believes the First Throne may have been escaping something beneath its civilisation, but has no definitive answer. ### Reported breach before Autumn Day 19 - The lower access was reportedly breached 11 nights before Autumn Day 19. - Watchmen heard three knocks and unfamiliar voices. - Edrik Voss said that “something came through”. - No verified description of a creature, person or object that crossed the boundary has been established. - The exact nature and location of the reported breach remain unknown. ### The western boundary wall — independent witness accounts Darrik Stonehand and Harnel gave separate accounts before comparing details. Darrik reported: - Three knocks beyond the western boundary wall, somewhere inside the sealed workings rather than the outer mountain wall. - The knocks were irregularly spaced: first knock, pause, quicker second knock, pause, third knock. - Faint whispering without discernible words after the third knock. - A brief scraping sound followed by silence. - A colder patch near old boundary markers. - He did not hear the low hum Harnel later described. Harnel reported: - The same irregular three knocks beyond the western wall. - No voices. - A faint scraping sound, though he was uncertain. - A cold draught a little north of the old boundary markers. - A low hum lasting approximately 3–4 seconds after checking the wall; he initially assumed ventilation. - A thin line of dust on the floor near the markers the following morning, not a pile. - He did not report hearing voices. Both said they checked the wall and found no visible breach or loose masonry. Harnel had served watches for 11 years and had not heard similar knocks. Neither witness had a definitive explanation. ### Western wall inspection findings A non-invasive examination was authorised: visual inspection, measurements, resonance and temperature readings only. No drilling, masonry removal or disturbance of markers. - Darrik indicated a cold spot just north of a dark iron marker; Harnel marked a position farther north. - Orsa measured a different resonance response and lower surface temperature near the northern marker, with a weaker but measurable difference between the two markers. - Feldin observed differing masonry joints and a section that appeared slightly thicker behind the wall. Possible explanations include old repair, reinforcement or a construction void; there is not enough evidence to call it a doorway. - The markers are deeply seated and appear deliberately positioned relative to the masonry. Their purpose is unknown; they could be survey points, property markers, excavation limits or structural references. - Original construction plans and the upper workings survey do not show the two markers. - Rennik said earlier Royal Mining Office equipment concentrated on eastern access and lower inspection points, with no instructions to investigate the markers. ### Resonance observations and limits - A first simultaneous test showed a slight western fluctuation followed by a drainage-gauge change. The possible correspondence was not close enough to establish synchronisation. - A second test showed two drainage fluctuations and one western fluctuation. One drainage change preceded a western change by several seconds; another had no corresponding western response. - Orsa judged that both locations showed intermittent activity and occasional possible correspondence, but no consistent pattern. - Gloin perceived something like a disturbance passing through surrounding structure, but could not establish its direction. - Ordinary explanations still require examination: machinery, geological movement, water pressure, natural fractures, ventilation and moisture. - Rennik said no scheduled pumping was taking place in that section that day. Maintenance records still need checking. - Some moisture was present at a lower joint. These observations do not prove a connected network, a magical signal or a conscious response. ### Drainage replacement stone and workshop granite At an old drainage channel, the vibration was strongest at one replacement stone and weaker in a nearby pillar, floor and opposite wall. It was intermittent at roughly 19–21-second intervals, not perfectly regular. The replacement stone appeared dark charcoal-grey, almost black, with faint metallic-looking grain. It was smoother than surrounding masonry, with older mortar around it. Orsa documented a faint straight line across its surface, judged to look deliberately cut rather than like a natural fracture. The team did not clean, scrape, move or remove it. Gloin noticed a resemblance between this mine stone and the pale-grey granite retaining stone outside Maela's Silver Anvil workshop. These are not established as the same material: - The mine drainage replacement stone is dark charcoal-grey. - The Silver Anvil retaining stone is pale-grey northern foothills granite. - Maela also has a separate dark Ironspine stone sample. Maela said the workshop granite came from an old quarry in the northern Ironspine foothills. She agreed to retrieve old supplier records and provide the quarry name, current ownership and route. None has yet been established. ### Older maintenance register Rennik found a maintenance register dated 18 years earlier: - A western boundary temperature difference had been reported. - No water ingress was recorded. - The masonry was judged structurally sound. - No repairs were authorised. - A bottom note reads: “Further investigation deferred pending technical assessment.” - The signature is an office designation, Eastern Works Administration. The individual signature is difficult to read and appears to begin with R, but Rennik refused to guess. The administrative index and correspondence may identify who deferred the investigation. The identity is unknown. ### Other physical anomalies from the inspection - An older rectangular masonry infill behind a tool rack differs from surrounding wall masonry. No handles or hinges were visible. It could be an old repair, sealed opening or reinforcement; no conclusion was reached. - Borin's old survey shows that section as solid wall, not a doorway, but the recorded thickness appears greater than Feldin's present measurement by about a dwarf forearm. This could be survey error or an old alteration. - A faint resonance was measured at a lower corner, within uncertain range. - Several side passages differ: one blocked with relatively modern masonry, one behind a deteriorated timber barrier, and one carefully fitted with stone blocks. Their purposes are unknown. - Some lower workings have been closed for decades and are not routinely maintained. The last comprehensive structural survey was about 18 years old and covered only upper workings. ### Royal Mining Office and political context - Royal Mining Office equipment at the site included measuring instruments, resonance detection equipment and three portable rune-binding frames. - Maela explained that the frames hold rune components fixed during energy transfer and could stabilise or reconnect components. Their presence does not prove that the Office knows how to operate the First Throne containment system. - A sealed case was also present; its contents are unknown. - Edrik Voss said the Crown wanted the matter contained and that King Durgan IV had not been informed. This is an unverified statement from Edrik, not established fact. - Lord Chancellor Veyron is handling the investigation privately. No proof of conspiracy or deliberate wrongdoing by the Crown, the Office or the Chancellor has been established. - A fourth unknown official was reportedly present during the original sealing: tall for a dwarf, dark beard, silver insignia crossed hammer/narrow tower, accompanied by two guards, no tools. He argued with Thrain, who said: “You were not authorised to touch it.” The official's identity is unknown; a possible connection to Varric Stonehelm remains unproven. Borin places the argument outside the lower access. He drew the insignia and gave the sketch to Gloin. Its current custody has not been separately checked. ## Historical repository, Dorin Blackmantle and Varric Stonehelm ### Dorin Blackmantle's trail The repository investigation has identified Dorin Blackmantle's dated Crownward entry (14th day of Winter, Year 3,784), six weeks after Orik disappeared, with the former Chancellor's administrative offices recorded as his destination. No departure record survives. Hadrik also identified the missing restricted report, Assessment of the Eastern Substructure — Restricted. Its recorded author was Thrain Coppervein, reviewing authority Dorin Blackmantle, commissioning body the Royal Mining Office; final approval is unrecorded. The full discovery sequence and source context are preserved in the Campaign Chronicle — Gloin Hammerfeld. The report's contents and whether another copy survives remain unknown. ### Varric Stonehelm and the private repository Varric Stonehelm's established role and the repository transfer are summarised here; the dated discovery and its full chronology are recorded in the Campaign Chronicle — Gloin Hammerfeld. Varric was Examiner-General during the old sealing and authorised Dorin's access to the former Chancellor's administrative offices. Evidence indicates he ordered records transferred to a private repository beneath the old Crownward administrative quarter in the months after the mine was sealed. The repository reportedly closed 41 years ago. A surviving access-register copy lists Varric, an unidentified administrative custodian and a third deliberately obscured name. Hadrik still needs to establish whether the original register survives and whether access is safe. The repository may contain relevant records, but that is unconfirmed. - Gloin borrowed The Foundations of First Throne Script from Hadrik. - Gloin has not told Hadrik about his Common/Natural Magic harmonisation hypothesis and does not want Hadrik involved in Elska's separate research unless he chooses otherwise. ### Political context and limits of inference - Edrik Voss said the eastern mine investigation was being handled under Lord Chancellor Veyron's authority. - Edrik said King Durgan IV had not been informed. This has not been independently confirmed. - The Royal Mining Office sought Borin's original survey; Borin denied possessing it. The original survey remains with Borin. - Veyron's office ordered reviews of restricted First Throne historical material. - The Chancellor's motives are unknown. Secrecy may conceal misconduct, or may reflect an effort to contain a genuine danger. Neither interpretation is proven. - No conspiracy, deliberate Crown wrongdoing or attempt to release anything has been established. ## Quarry and stone-sample research Maela's workshop has four distinct samples: 1. Pale-grey northern foothills granite, the same type as the Silver Anvil retaining stone. 2. Dark dense Ironspine stone, charcoal-coloured with fine irregular grain; exact source unknown, acquired from a stoneworker. 3. Reddish mineral-bearing rock from an old foundation near the central Ironspine passes; source details limited and mineral inclusions unevenly distributed. 4. Fine-grained black stone from an uncertain original location; unusually uniform, origin and whether natural or treated unknown. Gloin tested the dark Ironspine sample with three gentle taps and Deepcraft sensing. He perceived unusual density, a faint sensation beneath the physical structure and a delayed deeper sensation after the taps, which he experienced as contained within the stone. Maela's gauge showed no significant corresponding fluctuation. The observations were recorded; the test was stopped. Gloin then repeated his earlier experiment on the pale-grey granite retaining stone outside the Silver Anvil. He sensed a narrow internal seam and faint irregularity, followed by a stronger deeper tremor. For a brief moment he felt something extending beyond the stone, as if the stone were part of something larger. He described it as if the sensation reached out to him rather than merely responding to his touch. He felt warmth that seemed comforting or welcoming and wanted to leave the stone alone and test again later. Maela recorded warmth, recognition and welcome as Gloin's impressions, not proof of awareness. She mentioned ambiguous ancient accounts of an “echo beneath the stone” and a First Throne excavation runesmith who claimed the mountain answered his presence. The account is brief and ambiguous; older stone-listening traditions are often treated symbolically. Maela had never encountered a reliable account of welcome or recognition. Open questions: Are the sensations physical resonance, Deepcraft perception, Natural Magic, an unknown property of the stone, or something else? Are the samples related? Is any apparent response conscious? None is established. ## Other sealed sites known from Maela's records Maela knows of three other sealed or poorly documented sites from records, but has not personally inspected them: - Karak-Dûm, western approaches: An old sealed underground complex with regular masonry; purpose disputed. - Karak-Thol, northern galleries: Unfamiliar masonry and mineral deposits exposed during excavation; work halted and galleries closed. - Abandoned fortress near the central Ironspine passes: An old architectural reference mentions a subterranean structure beneath the foundations; very little documentation survives. These are independent leads. Do not assume they are connected to one another, the eastern mine or the First Throne without evidence. ## Active research assignments and next steps | Lead | Responsible person | Status | | --- | --- | --- | | Confirm repository register and obscured name; assess safety | Hadrik Ironvein | Needs another day | | Retrieve supplier records for Silver Anvil granite and provide quarry name and route | Maela Deepforge | Promised; not yet completed | | Obtain the 18-year-old mine structural survey | Rennik Varn | Requested; delivery not guaranteed | | Investigate the drainage channel stone's replacement and maintenance history | Rennik / mine staff | Requested; unresolved | | Continue periodic resonance readings | Orsa | Requested; no causal conclusion | | Research historical Natural/Common Magic as an intermediary between disciplines | Elska Hammerfeld | Agreed; not yet begun; report to Gloin first | | Continue supervised Deepcraft direction training | Maela and Gloin | Planned; not yet completed | | Obtain administrative index and correspondence for the deferred western wall assessment | Mine administration / Rennik | Needed; no result yet | ## Independent mystery seeds elsewhere in Eryndor These are future discovery concepts, not events that have happened: - Khazari — The Kingdom Beneath the Kingdom. - Urakai — The Empire That Wasn't Supposed to Exist. - Sahrad — The Buried Fleet. - Southern Sultanates — The Sleeping Sun. - Gnomes — The Impossible Engine. - Giants of Tharvorn — The Walking Mountains. - The Library Without a Location. - The Inland Ocean — revised owner direction 21 November 2026: a huge concealed inland sea/lake surrounded by a loose broken ring of Avarran mountains, familiar to Khazari and a few shore communities but hidden from much of the wider world; some magical aspect is present, its mechanism and any deeper ruin/sea connections intentionally unknown. New possible lead: one moon might interact with the sea's local planetary Natural Magic, potentially influencing concealment, but no moon, discipline or cause has been identified or made canon. The older entirely-subterranean version is undergoing reconciliation; no completed discovery, public revelation or player knowledge gain. - The Fallen Star. - The City That Was Never Built. Their origins and explanations remain unknown. They need not share a common cause, civilisation or magical system. ## Cross-reference and campaign pause The dated sequence of discoveries, inspections, interviews, conversations and decisions is reserved for the Campaign Chronicle. This page is the current issue register, not a substitute timeline. At the current pause, Gloin and Maela have arrived at Hadrik Ironvein's desk in the Royal Historical Archive, Karak-Varn, at approximately 11:25 AM on Autumn Day 22, Year 3,847. Hadrik has asked what they have uncovered. Gloin has not yet answered. No time passes while paused. ## Authority seal and attunement-mark detail from the original World Bible The original survey interpretation records an attunement mark alongside the three concentric mechanisms: a small iron key enclosed within a circle. According to that interpretation, the authority mechanism cannot function properly without it. The source does not establish whether the original builders removed this mark before the sealing or whether someone removed it later. The Hammer and Crown is described in the original reference as a First Throne authority seal, older than the current Stonehand dynasty. It was once used to authorise magical mechanisms across the First Throne and was functional, not merely ceremonial. A possible interpretation is that the foundation, pressure distribution and containment barrier could continue functioning without the authority piece, while the missing component governs who can command the system rather than supplying its power. This remains an interpretation, not proof of the present state of the chamber. Do not assume the object Borin remembers is definitively the attunement key, that the mark and the authority piece are necessarily identical, or that reinserting anything would open the door. ### Old Quarry Access — newly recovered date and first-hand inspection sequence Earlier Eryndor campaign chronology places the visit by Gloin and Borin on Autumn Day 20, approximately 7:00–8:35 AM, followed by breakfast at 8:40 AM. This is a date attribution from prior campaign chronology, not newly supplied full verbatim dialogue. During an engineering lesson in three old quarry tunnel sections, Gloin learned to inspect roof fractures and dampness (7:05), support pillars (7:18) and timber supports (7:26). From 7:48–8:35 they examined the previously documented survey marker, markings and measurements. Borin compared a symbol to a drawing from the separate eastern mine. Distinction: Old Quarry Access is not the sealed eastern mine; no successful entry into the eastern mine is established for this morning. Neither is this necessarily the unnamed northern Ironspine foothills quarry that supplied Maela's Silver Anvil granite. The marker's displacement and any resonance/listening-network link remain unexplained. ## First Throne listening network and old-quarry evidence Gloin's reading of The Foundations of First Throne Script revealed a diagram showing listening stations connected by rune lines. Maela believes the diagram may represent a network of resonance anchors monitoring large underground systems. This is her interpretation of the diagram, not proof that the network still operates or that any particular sites are connected. At an old quarry, Gloin and Borin found: - A survey marker whose modern outer measurements remained intact while older First Throne geometric symbols lay beneath them. - The marker had been deliberately repositioned; the reason is unknown. - A timber support bore a symbol of three vertical lines and a circular mark. - Maela considers the symbol consistent with a resonance-transfer system and likely more than a simple structural mark. - Borin suspects the quarry marker may belong to a wider listening network and thinks someone may have shifted it to conceal what it measured. This is a hypothesis, not an established motive. Keep this old-quarry evidence distinct from the four stone samples at Maela's Silver Anvil and from the still-unnamed northern Ironspine foothills quarry that supplied her workshop granite. Do not assume they are the same quarry or part of one confirmed system. ## Original inspection contract, planned personnel and equipment The original mine-inspection arrangement recorded that Lord Chancellor Veyron's office requested Maela inspect the ancient containment runes. Maela accepted subject to two conditions: 1. Access to surviving architectural records. 2. Permission to inspect the surrounding structure before touching any ancient runes. The office refused to explain the reported breach in writing. Maela intended to honour the agreement but would stop if the structure was unsafe or containment might be compromised. She would not activate or alter a mechanism she did not understand. The inspection was scheduled for first light on Autumn Day 22 at the eastern access. The original planned party was: - Maela Deepforge, specialist in ancient runic architecture. - Edrik Voss, Deputy Examiner of the Royal Mining Office. - Captain Roderic Vale, commander of the assigned royal security detail. Maela had not worked with Captain Vale and did not know whether his role was protection, supervision or enforcement. Continuity note: The later Day 22 inspection chronicle records Maela, site supervisor Rennik Varn, structural assessor Feldin, resonance/material assessor Orsa and Gloin as the people present for the inspection. It does not explain the status or absence of Edrik Voss and Captain Roderic Vale. Preserve both the original planned roster and the actual recorded attendees; do not invent a cancellation, substitution or explanation. The equipment list supplied to Maela included: - Structural measuring instruments. - Resonance-detection equipment. - Three portable rune-binding frames. - Heavy iron lifting apparatus. - A sealed wooden case listed only as “authorised technical materials”. Maela explained that rune-binding frames hold components in fixed alignment while energy transfers between them. They are used legitimately for restoration, stabilising damaged mechanisms and constructing bindings, but could also reconnect components that were deliberately separated. The sealed case's contents were unknown. Hadrik wanted to learn who authorised its transport and who had custody. No evidence established malicious intent. The equipment list and the unexplained sealed case should remain distinct from the instruments and gauges actually documented during the Day 22 non-invasive inspection.
